Subject: Console DPA quickcards for onboarding — short public snippets review

Team / Sarah —

We're putting together a small set of "quickcards" that will live in the Console onboarding flow for new customers. The goal is a) give procurement/legal folks a one-sentence summary of our DPA/subprocessor/data transfer posture, and b) offer a slightly longer 1–2 line tooltip for engineers.

Attached is DPA_quickcard_v1.pdf (two variants) and a tiny diff of console copy (console-snippet-diff.md). We need legal sign-off on the one-sentence copy and product sign-off on the tooltip length/placement. Sarah, sharing early since Acme onboarding team asked for a short blurb we can paste into our internal procurement notes.

Items we want to resolve in this thread:
- Final one-sentence public-facing statement about subprocessors and cross-border transfers (aiming for ~18–20 words).
- 1–2 line tooltip for Console where we can point customers for more detail.
- Confirm whether we need to list EU data center locations explicitly in the onboarding card or link to the subprocessor map.

Quick take (draft) in the PDF: "Redwood uses a limited set of subprocessors for infrastructure and logging; cross-border transfers are covered under our DPA with standard safeguards. See Details."

Please reply with edits inline or propose alternative one-liners (no legalese, customer-friendly).

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Developer GTM, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Console DPA quickcards for onboarding — short public snippets review

Laura —

Thanks for the draft. This is a useful customer UX idea. A couple of legal notes and a proposed streamlined sentence for the public card:

1) One-sentence public blurb (legal-clean, customer-friendly):
"We use a small, vetted set of subprocessors for infrastructure and monitoring; transfers outside the EEA are covered by our DPA and standard safeguards."

Rationale: avoids the word "logging" (too specific) and keeps it high-level. "Transfers outside the EEA" is clearer for customers in procurement than a generic "cross-border transfers."

2) Tooltip (1–2 lines) for engineers:
"Redwood processes requests in regional capacity pools. We may route data to subprocessors for performance and reliability. See full subprocessor map and transfer details."

3) Subprocessor listing in the onboarding card: don't list full locations in the card — link to the subprocessor map. If a customer explicitly requests EU-only routing we support that via Dedicated/Private options and that's a sales/procurement conversation.

4) Minor redlines in the PDF: remove any phrase implying we retain raw customer prompts beyond customer-chosen retention settings. Also replace "standard safeguards" with "standard contractual safeguards (e.g., SCCs)" if you want precision, but that might be too legal-heavy for onboarding.

If Marketing prefers an even shorter public sentence, swap "transfers outside the EEA" to "data transfers are covered by our DPA."

Happy to approve once we agree wording.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Thanks Kim and Laura —

From a Console/product perspective, a few pragmatic constraints and suggestions:
- Tooltip length: aim for one line in the card with a "Learn more" chevron that expands a 2–3 line paragraph (not a full modal). That keeps onboarding flow light.
- Link target: use the subprocessor map + a short anchor on the privacy page (e.g., /privacy#subprocessors). Avoid Drive links for production.
- UX copy variants: we should prepare two variants — "procurement friendly" (simple, slightly formal) and "engineer friendly" (technical, mentions routing and capacity pools). The product can swap by role detection in the Console (admin vs. developer).
- EU center mention: do not hardcode region names. Instead show a small link "Data regions & residency" that opens the residency settings page where we can show EU/US APAC locations.

I've uploaded an implementation stub for the Console team (console-snippet-diff.md) and linked to the UI mock in the Drive link. Marcus, can you confirm the expanded paragraph won't exceed our allowed 280px card height? If so we can ship both variants.

Priya

If you can give us a short confirmed sentence we can paste it into our onboarding checklist. Otherwise procurement will request a short addendum in the SOW.
